name: 玉门关口
Yumen Gate
before: 玉门关的城门洞开着，门洞里却横着一根拴马桩。几个沙匪刀手戴着从关吏头上扒下来的乌纱帽，挨个向出关的人收「出关钱」：一人一百文，骡马加倍，哭的另算。关楼上的老更夫缩在箭窗里冲你们直摆手。门外就是关外，风里一股沙子的味道。

The gate of Yumen Pass stands open, yet a hitching post bars the archway. A few sand-bandit blades in a toll officer's stolen cap are charging everyone who leaves: a hundred coins a head, double for mules, extra if you cry. The old night watchman hides in an arrow slit and waves you away. Beyond the gate lies the frontier, and the wind smells of sand.
after: 乌纱帽滚进了沟里，拴马桩劈了当柴。老更夫爬下关楼，举着灯笼照门洞里的一块砖：一行刀刻的小字，「丁未年三月，千里号出关，三百人」。他说十年来出关的人不少，可走这条路去西边做大买卖的，你们是头一支。

The cap rolls into the ditch and the post becomes firewood. The watchman climbs down and holds his lantern to a brick in the archway, where a knife has cut a line of small characters: 'Third month, Dingwei year. The Qianli caravan went out. Three hundred souls.' Plenty of people have left by this gate in ten years, he says, but you are the first to take this road west to trade since then.

name: 折柳亭
Willow Pavilion
before: 关外第一座亭子叫折柳亭，亭边一棵老柳，枝上系满了褪色的布条：出关的人系一条布，盼着回来时还认得这里。今天一伙兵痞拎着斧头在砍树，说「烧火正好，反正没几个人回来」。一个卖香烛的老太太抱着树干，死活不撒手。

The first pavilion outside the pass has an old willow beside it, its branches heavy with faded strips of cloth: everyone who leaves ties one, hoping to know the place again on the way home. Today a gang of rogue soldiers is hacking at the trunk. 'Good firewood,' they say, 'hardly anyone comes back anyway.' An old woman who sells incense hugs the tree and will not let go.
after: 兵痞们丢下斧头跑了。老太太指给你们看最高的那根枝：上面密密麻麻系着三百条一样的红布，同一天系的，一条都没解下来过。「千里号的。」她说，「系布的人回来，要自己解。」她又塞给你们一条蓝布。

The soldiers drop their axes and run. The old woman points to the highest branch: three hundred identical red strips, tied on the same day, not one ever untied. 'The Qianli caravan's,' she says. 'Whoever ties a cloth has to come back and untie it himself.' Then she presses a strip of blue cloth into your hands.

name: 骰子坡
Dice Slope
before: 坡上蹲着一伙从关里逃债出来的赌鬼，入了沙匪的伙。他们开了个赌局，赌的是你们：「开拓队能不能活着回来」，一赔三百。谁不肯下注就抢谁。领头的拿着一本油腻的赌簿，见了你们的旗子，眼睛一亮：「正主来了！」

A gang of gamblers who fled their debts inside the pass has joined the sand bandits. They're running a book, and the bet is you: 'Will the pioneers come back alive?' Odds: three hundred to one. Anyone who won't bet gets robbed. Their leader clutches a greasy betting ledger, and his eyes light up at your banner: 'The horse itself has arrived!'
after: 灌了铅的骰子被一脚踩进沙里，赌簿归了你们。翻到最前面，是十年前开的一局：「千里号回不回」，押「回」的只有一个人，签名是一把小算盘。领头的嘟囔：「那人押了自己，到现在也没来收钱。」

The loaded dice get stamped into the sand and the betting book is yours. On its first page is a bet from ten years ago: 'Will the Qianli caravan come back?' Only one person bet 'yes', and he signed with a little abacus. 'That fellow bet on himself,' the leader mutters, 'and he's never come to collect.'

name: 响铃坡
Bell Slope
before: 古道在这里翻一道缓坡，坡顶一伙大漠响马把抢来的铃铛挂满了一棵枯树，风一吹叮当乱响，远远就能听见。他们每劫一队就摘一个铃铛当战利品。树上少说挂了六七十个，最老的一个锈得只剩半边，响马说那一个不是抢的，是在沙里捡的。

The old road climbs a gentle slope here, and on the crest a band of desert raiders has hung their stolen bells all over a dead tree. When the wind blows they clang so loudly you hear them from far off. Every caravan they rob gives up one bell as a trophy. There must be sixty or seventy on the tree; the oldest, rusted to half a shell, they say wasn't stolen but found in the sand.
after: 响马散了，你们把铃铛一个个摘下来，等失主来认。那个锈了半边的铜铃上铸着一个「千」字，铃舌早没了，摇起来一声不响。一个过路的老脚夫说，十年前出关的那支商队，铃铛都是这样的。

The raiders scatter and you take the bells down for their owners to claim. The half-rusted one is cast with the character Qian. Its clapper is gone, and it makes no sound when shaken. An old porter passing by says the caravan that went out ten years ago had bells exactly like it.

name: 挪步碑
Wandering Milestone
before: 路边一块里程碑，「西去阳关一百二十里」。附近的人都说这碑每晚往西挪一步，是在追十年前那支商队。一个疯道士带着十几个信徒围着碑磕头，自称「随石教」，向过路人收「随喜钱」，不给的就被信徒们按在碑前磕满一百个头。

A milestone by the road reads 'Yangguan, 120 li west'. The locals say it moves one step west every night, chasing the caravan that left ten years ago. A mad Taoist and a dozen followers kowtow around it, calling themselves the Followers of the Stone, and collect 'offerings' from travellers. Anyone who won't pay is held down to knock his head on the stone a hundred times.
after: 信徒们一哄而散，夜里你们守着碑，果然看见那疯道士偷偷撬着碑往西挪。可碑座底下露出来的东西让人愣住：三百道细细的刻痕，每道旁边一个小字，是名字的头一个字。疯道士说，他只是想让它们离西边近一点。

The followers scatter. That night you watch the stone and catch the mad Taoist levering it a step west. But what the moved base reveals stops you short: three hundred fine notches, each with one small character beside it, the first character of a name. The Taoist says he only wanted to bring them a little closer to the west.

name: 逃兵屯
Deserters' Camp
before: 一大片土坯房，住着上百个从边军里逃出来的兵痞。他们占了屯田，自封「关外第一营」，每天照样点卯、操练、吹号，就是不打仗，只向过路的商人征「军饷」。营门口贴着一张告示，错字比字还多，落款写的却是「千里号护卫营」。

A sprawl of mud-brick huts holds more than a hundred deserters from the border army. They've seized the farmland, named themselves 'First Battalion Beyond the Pass', and still muster, drill and sound the horn every day; they just never fight, and collect 'army pay' from passing merchants. The notice on their gate has more wrong characters than right ones, and it is signed 'Qianli Caravan Escort Battalion'.
after: 号角吹到一半就哑了。降兵里一个老卒红着脸说：十年前他们这营本是派去护送千里号的，出发前一夜一纸调令撤了，商队自己走了。「后来听说一个都没回来，我们就……没脸回营了。」屯田还给了庄户，那张告示你们留着。

The horn dies mid-call. An old soldier among the surrendered says, red-faced, that ten years ago this unit was assigned to escort the Qianli caravan. The night before they set out, an order came cancelling it, and the caravan left on its own. 'Then we heard not one came back, and we... couldn't face going back to camp.' The fields go back to the farmers. You keep the notice.

name: 头道驿
First Post Station
before: 出关后的头一座驿站被一伙沙匪围了三天。驿卒们用桌椅堵住大门，死守着一只封了火漆的公文筒，说是朝廷的急递，只交给「开拓队」。沙匪以为筒里是银票，一边撞门一边喊：「交出来就放你们走！」门板上已经插满了箭。

The first post station beyond the pass has been besieged by sand bandits for three days. The clerks have barricaded the door with tables and chairs and are guarding a wax-sealed dispatch tube: an urgent court message, they say, to be handed only to 'the pioneers'. The bandits think it's full of banknotes and keep battering the door, yelling 'hand it over and we'll let you go!' The door bristles with arrows.
after: 沙匪被打散，驿卒们开门把公文筒交到你们手里。里面是朝廷发给沿路的告示：「开拓队西行，沿途驿站照应，并访千里号下落。」老驿卒说，十年前也来过一份差不多的，只是那份上写的是「照应千里号」。

The bandits are scattered and the clerks open up and hand you the tube. Inside is a court notice to every station on the road: 'The pioneers travel west. Stations are to assist them, and to seek news of the Qianli caravan.' The old clerk says a notice much like it came ten years ago, except that one said: 'Assist the Qianli caravan.'
first: 沙匪营里抄出四十袋小米、两缸腌肉、一捆崭新的马鞭、十几把撞门撞弯了的铁锤，还有一张画着驿站的草图，标着「银子在此」。
The bandit camp yields forty sacks of millet, two jars of salted meat, a bundle of new whips, a dozen sledgehammers bent from battering the door, and a sketch of the station marked 'silver here'.
pass: 驿卒们每次都把最新的塘报念给你们听，驿卒老婆烤好芝麻馕塞进鞍袋，还替你们把磨破的旗角缝好。
The clerks read you the latest bulletins every time, the clerk's wife slips fresh sesame flatbreads into your saddlebags, and someone always mends the frayed corner of your banner.

name: 六岔口
Six-Way Fork
before: 六条小路在这里散开，路口坐着个摆摊算卦的「六路先生」。他自己承认是个骗子，卦签都是瞎抽的，可怪就怪在每回都准。一伙沙匪把他绑在路口，逼他算哪一路商队有钱，算得太准，沙匪抢得太顺，附近的商人都快绝迹了。

Six tracks fan out here, and at the fork sits a fortune-teller called Master Six Roads. He freely admits he's a fraud who draws his sticks at random, yet strangely he's always right. A gang of sand bandits has tied him up at the fork and makes him predict which caravans are worth robbing. He's so accurate and they rob so well that merchants have nearly vanished from these parts.
after: 绳子一松，六路先生顺手给你们抽了一签，看了半天，哆嗦着说：「往西有人跟你们要一本账，再往西，有个只剩一只眼的人在等你们问话。」他说这卦他不收钱，太准了，怕。

Untied, Master Six Roads draws a stick for you out of habit, stares at it a long while, then says shakily: 'Out west, people will ask you for a ledger. Further west, a man with only one eye is waiting for you to ask him a question.' He won't take a coin for this one. It's too accurate. It frightens him.

name: 灰眼胡商帐
Grey-Eyed Trader's Tent
before: 一顶缀满铜片的大帐，主人是个灰眼睛的胡商，大胡子编成三股。他只收货，不收铜钱，说铜钱「到了关外就是废铁」。他也不跟软脚虾做生意：想进他的帐，得先赢过他雇的那几个刀手。他坐在帐门口嗑瓜子，看得津津有味。

A big tent stitched with copper discs belongs to a grey-eyed foreign trader with a beard in three braids. He takes goods, never coins: 'beyond the pass, copper is scrap'. Nor does he deal with weaklings. To enter his tent you must first beat his hired blades, and he sits at the flap cracking melon seeds, enjoying the show.
after: 最后一个刀手躺倒，胡商哈哈大笑，掀帘请你们进去换货。帐角压着一摞落了灰的毡帽。「十年前一个拿算盘的人订了三百顶，付了一半。他自己当场戴走一顶，说剩下的回来再取。」胡商数给你们看：二百九十九顶。「别的货随便换，这些不行。」

The last blade goes down. The trader roars with laughter and holds the flap open for you to trade. In a corner sits a dusty stack of felt hats. 'Ten years ago a man with an abacus ordered three hundred and paid half. He put one on there and then, and said he'd collect the rest on the way back.' He counts them for you: two hundred and ninety-nine. 'Trade for anything else you like. Not these.'

name: 唱曲墩
Singer's Mound
before: 土墩下坐着一个瞎眼的老琴师，拉着一把蒙羊皮的胡琴，唱一支谁也没听过的曲子：「三百人出关去，账房先生点灯数……」一伙兵痞围着他踢翻了他的碗，说这曲子晦气，不许再唱。老琴师偏不停，弦断了一根，接着唱。

Under a mound of earth sits a blind old fiddler, singing a song nobody has heard: 'Three hundred went out past the gate, the bookkeeper lit a lamp and counted...' A gang of rogue soldiers kicks over his bowl and says the song is bad luck. He keeps singing. A string snaps; he sings on.
after: 兵痞们跑了，老琴师换上新弦，把整支曲子唱给你们听。最后一句是「灯数到二百九十九，账房先生不肯走」。问他从哪儿学的，他说是十年前一个伙计教的，那伙计说，路上有人记账，回来时要听他唱全。

The soldiers gone, the old man restrings and sings you the whole song. The last line: 'The lamp counted two hundred and ninety-nine, and the bookkeeper would not leave.' He learned it ten years ago from a caravan hand, he says, who told him someone on the road was keeping accounts, and he must sing it whole when they came back.

name: 喜轿沟
Bridal Gully
before: 沟里停着一顶花轿，新娘子在里头哭。一个恶霸的家丁拦住了送亲的队伍，不要钱，要嫁妆箱子里的一张纸，说那张纸「值一头骆驼」。新郎官是个放鹰的小伙子，正撸起袖子准备拼命，新娘在轿子里喊：「那是我爹留给我的！」

A bridal sedan stands in the gully and the bride inside is crying. A bully's thugs have stopped the wedding party. They don't want money; they want one sheet of paper from the dowry chest, which they say is 'worth a camel'. The groom, a young falconer, is rolling up his sleeves to fight to the death, and the bride cries from the sedan: 'My father left me that!'
after: 家丁被打跑了。新娘掀开轿帘，把那张纸给你们看：一张欠条，「借驼一头，归时奉还，千里号」，落款盖着一枚小算盘印。她爹等了十年没等到，就把它当了嫁妆。「上头说归时还，」她笑着说，「我嫁了，它也跟着我等。」

The thugs are driven off. The bride lifts the curtain and shows you the paper: an IOU, 'One camel borrowed, to be returned on our way back. Qianli caravan', stamped with a little abacus seal. Her father waited ten years and in the end made it part of her dowry. 'It says it'll be returned,' she says with a smile. 'I'm married now. It can wait with me.'

name: 正午坡
Noon Slope
before: 坡顶站着一个抱刀的沙匪，每天正午拦住一个过路人比刀，输了留下兵器，赢了……还没人赢过。他说十年前就在这里输给过一个人，那人是一支大商队的护卫头，刀法比他快半拍，赢了也不要他的命，只说「回来再比」。他从那天起每天正午都在等。

A sand bandit stands on the crest with a sword in his arms. Every noon he stops one traveller to duel; losers leave their weapons, and nobody has ever won. Ten years ago, he says, he lost here to a man, the guard captain of a great caravan, half a beat faster than him, who spared his life and said only, 'Again when I come back.' He has waited every noon since.
after: 刀客输了，坐在坡上半天没说话，然后把一截断刀尖递给你们：那是当年护卫头的刀，比刀时崩下来的，上面刻着「千里号」。「他没回来，」刀客说，「那就你们替他回来，下回我们再比。」

The swordsman loses and sits on the slope a long time without a word. Then he hands you a broken sword tip: it chipped off the guard captain's blade in their duel, and it's engraved 'Qianli'. 'He never came back,' says the swordsman. 'So you come back in his place, and we'll duel again.'

name: 错银车
Silver That Wasn't
before: 一伙沙匪抢了一辆牛车，车上码着一块块白亮亮的砖，以为是银锭，乐得在车边跳舞。可他们用刀砍、用火烧，「银子」就是不化，有个沙匪舔了一口，咸得直吐。他们不肯认，硬说是银子成了精，押着赶车的老汉要他「把银子变回来」。

A gang of sand bandits has robbed an ox cart stacked with bright white bricks they took for silver ingots, and danced around it for joy. But chop or burn them as they will, the 'silver' won't melt, and one bandit who licked it spat for a full minute: salty. They refuse to admit it and insist the silver has turned into a demon, ordering the old carter to 'change it back'.
after: 沙匪被打跑了。老汉说这车不是银也不是普通的盐，是他每年往西边送的「回程盐」：十年前千里号走时在他这儿订的，一年一车，埋在沿路的石堆底下，等他们回程时吃。砖上都压着一枚小算盘印。「钱付了十年的，」老汉说，「今年是最后一车。」

The bandits are driven off. The carter explains it's neither silver nor ordinary salt but his yearly load of 'homeward salt': ordered ten years ago by the Qianli caravan, one cartload a year, buried under cairns along the road for them to eat on their way home. Each brick bears a little abacus seal. 'They paid for ten years,' the old man says. 'This year's the last load.'

name: 节日梁
Feast-Day Ridge
before: 这伙大漠响马有条祖传的规矩：只在过节的日子打劫，平时种地。可今年的节不够用了，他们自己发明了一个：「开拓队出关节」，今天就是。全伙人穿上了过年的新衣裳，在梁上贴了红纸，敲着锣等你们。

This band of desert raiders has an ancestral rule: they only rob on feast days, and farm the rest of the time. But this year there aren't enough feasts, so they've invented one: 'Pioneers Leave the Pass Day', which is today. The whole gang has put on New Year clothes, pasted red paper all over the ridge, and are banging a gong waiting for you.
after: 节过完了，响马们脱了新衣裳。老头领交出一只木匣：十年前也是过节，他们劫了千里号押尾的这只匣子，里面全是纸，三百个名字抄得工工整整。「那账房追回来要，说丢了副本要重抄一夜。我们没还，一直怪不好意思的。」

The feast is over and the raiders sheepishly take off their best clothes. The old chief hands over a wooden box. Ten years ago, also on a feast day, they robbed this box from the Qianli caravan's rearguard and found only paper: three hundred names, neatly copied. 'The bookkeeper rode back asking for it. Said it was the copy, and losing it meant a whole night writing it out again,' the chief says. 'We never returned it. Always felt a bit bad.'

name: 题壁墩
Poem Wall Tower
before: 长城在这里塌了一个豁口，一伙兵痞每天拆墙砖拉去关里卖。墙上写满了历代过客的题诗，一个瘦得像竹竿的穷诗人守在豁口，每拆一块砖，他就抢着把砖上的诗抄下来。今天兵痞们要拆的那块，他张开双臂护着，说那上面的两句他抄了十年也舍不得抄完。

The wall has a gap here, and a gang of rogue soldiers prises out its bricks to sell inside the pass. Its surface is covered in poems left by travellers through the ages, and a poor poet thin as a bamboo pole keeps watch at the gap, copying every poem before its brick is taken. Today he spreads his arms to shield one brick: its two lines, he says, he's been copying for ten years and can't bear to finish.
after: 兵痞们跑了，砖保住了。上面是两行小楷，字迹工整得像账簿：「一笔一笔算，一步一步还。」落款没有名字，只画了一把算盘。诗人说，这是他见过最不像诗的诗，也是他最喜欢的一首。

The soldiers flee and the brick is saved. On it are two lines in small, neat script, tidy as a ledger: 'Reckon it stroke by stroke; repay it step by step.' No name, only a little abacus drawn below. The poet says it's the least poetic poem he's ever seen, and his favourite.

name: 量沙台
Sand-Measuring Terrace
before: 一座土台上，一个穿长衫的书生拿着一根打了结的长绳，一绳一绳地量戈壁，要画一张从玉门到阳关的「丈量真图」，已经量了四年。昨天一伙沙匪抢了他的绳子去捆货，还把他的草稿垫了锅底。书生坐在台上哭得像个孩子，说最要紧的那一页也烧了。

On an earth terrace, a scholar in a long gown measures the gobi length by length with a knotted rope. He means to draw a 'True Survey Map' from Yumen to Yangguan and has been at it four years. Yesterday sand bandits stole his rope to tie up loot and lined their cooking pot with his drafts. He sits crying like a child: the most important page burned too.
after: 绳子抢回来了，那一页只烧掉一角。原来那不是他的稿子，是他在路边捡的一张旧纸，上面记着「玉门至阳关，三十一万四千步」，逐日记数，一步不差。书生说他量了四年，量出来的数跟这张纸只差一百步。「记这张纸的人，是一步一步数着走的。」

You recover the rope, and the page has lost only a corner. It turns out it isn't his draft but an old sheet he found by the road: 'Yumen to Yangguan, 314,000 paces', counted day by day. Four years of measuring, the scholar says, and his figure differs from it by only a hundred paces. 'Whoever wrote this counted every single step.'

name: 假关门
Fake Gate
before: 古道正中竖着一座木头牌坊，刷着三个大字「玉门关」，可玉门关明明在身后二十里。一伙沙匪刀手扮成守关兵，拿着木头刀查验文牒、征收关税，谁说「这不是玉门关」就挨一顿揍。不少外地商人真被唬住了，老老实实交了两回钱。

A wooden archway straddles the old road, painted 'Yumen Pass'. But Yumen Pass is twenty li behind you. A gang of sand-bandit blades dressed as gate guards checks papers and collects duty with wooden swords, and beats anyone who says 'this isn't Yumen Pass'. Plenty of strangers have been fooled into paying twice.
after: 牌坊被推倒了，砸起好大一片土。翻过那块写着「玉门关」的木板，背面还有一行旧漆：「千里号第三十七车」。沙匪说木板是在路边捡的大车板子。原来商队过了这里就开始拆车，把木头留在路上，换成骆驼进沙漠。

The archway comes down in a cloud of dust. On the back of the 'Yumen Pass' board is a line of old paint: 'Qianli caravan, cart no. 37'. The bandits say they found the planks by the road. It seems the caravan began breaking up its carts here, leaving the wood behind and switching to camels for the desert.

name: 锅灶梁
Cookpot Ridge
before: 梁上炊烟袅袅，肉香飘出好几里。一伙沙匪绑了关里酒楼的一个大厨，逼他天天给他们做饭，吃得一个个油光满面。大厨被拴在灶台边，一边炒菜一边偷偷往锅里多撒盐，想把他们齁跑，可他们越吃越爱吃。

Cooking smoke curls over the ridge and the smell of meat carries for miles. A gang of sand bandits has kidnapped a head chef from a restaurant inside the pass and makes him cook for them daily; they're all shiny with grease. Chained to the stove, he sneaks extra salt into every dish to drive them off. They only like it more.
after: 沙匪吃撑了跑不动，被一个个拎了出来。大厨给你们炒了一大锅菜，边炒边说：十年前千里号出关，送行宴是他掌的勺，三百份。临散席，账房先生又要了一碗，说「给后头来的人留着」。他摆上碗筷：「今天总算有人来吃了。」

The bandits have eaten too much to run and are hauled out one by one. The chef fries you a huge panful, talking as he cooks. Ten years ago he cooked the Qianli caravan's farewell banquet, three hundred portions. As it broke up, the bookkeeper asked for one more bowl: 'Save it for whoever comes after us.' He sets out the bowls. 'Today someone's finally come to eat it.'

name: 白骨驿
Bone Post Station
before: 驿站的院墙是用兽骨垒的，远看一片白，所以叫白骨驿。驿里只住着一个老驿丞，每天天一黑就点起十二盏灯，一盏不少，一夜不灭。一伙沙匪打听到他存着好几坛灯油，今晚来抢，老驿丞抱着油坛子站在灯前，说灯不能灭。

The courtyard walls are built of bleached bones, white from afar; hence the name. Only an old postmaster lives here, and every night at dusk he lights twelve lamps, never one fewer, and keeps them burning till dawn. Sand bandits have learned he stores jars of lamp oil and come to take them tonight. The old man stands before his lamps hugging an oil jar. The lamps, he says, must not go out.
after: 沙匪被赶出了骨墙，一盏灯也没灭。老驿丞翻开驿簿：「十年前千里号在这里歇过一夜，账房先生登了三百个名字，每人编了号。一盏灯照二十五个，十二盏，三百人。」可最后一盏灯下只有二十四个名字，第三百号空着，只写了「账房」。「他登了别人，就是不写自己。」

The bandits are driven beyond the bone walls and not one lamp goes out. The postmaster opens a yellowed register. 'Ten years ago the Qianli caravan rested here. Their bookkeeper entered every name, stroke by stroke, and gave each a number.' He points at the lamps. 'Each lamp lights twenty-five names. Twelve lamps, three hundred people.' But when you count, the last lamp has only twenty-four. Number three hundred is blank except for one word: 'Bookkeeper'. 'He entered everyone else,' the old man says, 'but never himself.'

name: 枣树界
Jujube Boundary
before: 两个村子之间长着一棵老枣树，正好在界上。东村说树是东村的，西村说枣子落在西村就是西村的。吵了十年，今年两边都花钱雇了沙匪来「评理」，结果沙匪把两村的人都绑了，枣子也摘光了，正坐在树下吐枣核。

An old jujube tree stands exactly on the boundary between two villages. East says the tree is theirs; West says fruit that falls on their side is theirs. After ten years of quarrelling, both sides hired sand bandits this year to 'settle it'. The bandits tied up both villages, stripped the tree, and are sitting under it spitting out stones.
after: 沙匪被打跑了。两个村长各从怀里掏出半张纸，一对，严丝合缝：是十年前路过的一位账房先生替他们写的公断，「单年东摘，双年西摘，树荫共用」，后来吵架撕成了两半。两个村长对着那把小算盘印，臊得说不出话。

The bandits flee. Each headman pulls half a sheet of paper from his coat, and the halves fit perfectly: a ruling written for them ten years ago by a passing bookkeeper, 'East picks in odd years, West in even; the shade is for all', torn in two in a later quarrel. Facing that little abacus seal, the headmen are too ashamed to speak.

name: 獭子洞
Marmot Burrows
before: 一片满是旱獭洞的荒坡。关外传开了一个谣言：千里号的账房在沿路埋了银子，记在账本上。一伙沙匪认定银子就在这片坡底下，天天趴在地上一个洞一个洞地掏，被獭子咬得满手牙印，还把路过的人抓来帮着掏。

A barren slope riddled with marmot burrows. A rumour has spread across the frontier: the Qianli caravan's bookkeeper buried silver along the road and recorded it in his ledger. A gang of sand bandits is convinced it's under this slope, and spends every day on their bellies digging out hole after hole, hands covered in marmot bites, press-ganging passers-by to help.
after: 沙匪被赶走了，你们没去掏洞，只在坡上插了块木牌：「此坡无银，獭子作证。」谣言却没停，往西去的路上，越来越多的人在找那本账本。
The bandits are run off. You don't dig; you just plant a sign: 'No silver here, the marmots will testify.' But the rumour doesn't stop. Further west, more and more people are looking for that ledger.

name: 沙狐窝
Sand Fox Dens
before: 北山脚下的乱石缝里住着一大窝沙狐，夜里成群下山偷鸡、叼肉干，还专偷亮晶晶的东西：铜扣、耳环、驿站的灯罩。牧民说这窝狐狸是「生不完的」：一窝刚赶走，石缝里又钻出一窝新的，每年开春都要请人来清一次。

In the rock crevices at the foot of the northern hills lives a clan of sand foxes. At night they come down to steal chickens and jerky, and anything shiny: brass buttons, earrings, the station's lamp glass. The herders say these foxes 'never run out': drive off one litter and another wriggles out, so every spring someone has to be hired to clear them.
after: 狐群被赶回了深山，石缝里掏出一窝亮晶晶的小玩意，其中有一颗铜算盘珠，刻着「千」字，不知道狐狸从哪儿叼来的。可你们离开时，石缝里又传出了小狐狸的叫声，过一阵还得再来清。

The foxes are driven back into the hills, and from the crevices you pull out a hoard of shiny trinkets, among them a brass abacus bead carved with Qian. Who knows where the foxes found it. But as you leave, new kits are already yipping in the rocks. You'll have to come back and clear them again.

name: 屯田仓
Garrison Granary
before: 这座粮仓本是给屯田庄户存种粮的。管事姓胡，勾结一伙兵痞锁了仓门，拿出一张「千里号欠条」，说十年前商队借了仓里的粮没还，这笔账要庄户们替他们还，种子三倍价钱。庄户们交不起，春耕眼看要误了。

This granary stores seed for the garrison farmers. Its steward, Hu, in league with a gang of rogue soldiers, has locked the doors and produced a 'Qianli caravan IOU': ten years ago the caravan borrowed grain and never repaid it, he says, so the farmers must pay the debt for them, with seed at triple price. They can't, and spring ploughing is slipping away.
after: 胡管事被请了下来，兵痞四散。那张欠条一看就是假的：没有算盘印。一个老庄户冷笑：「真欠条我家有一张，人家借的是一斗麦，还多给了一斗当利钱。」仓门大开，庄户们排着队领种子。

Steward Hu is hauled down and the soldiers scatter. The IOU is an obvious fake: no abacus seal. An old farmer snorts: 'My family has a real one. They borrowed one measure of wheat and left another as interest.' The doors are flung open and the farmers line up for seed.
first: 仓底抄出三百斗麦子、一箱铜钱、几十匹细布、一叠还没写完的假欠条，还有一把剑柄镶金、剑刃却是生锈铁片的佩剑。
Under the floor: three hundred measures of wheat, a chest of coins, dozens of bolts of fine cloth, a stack of half-written fake IOUs, and a sword with a gilded hilt and a blade of rusty iron.
pass: 庄户们每次都从地头跑过来，塞给你们一口袋新磨的麦面，还有一罐自家腌的韭菜花。
Every time you pass, a farmer runs over from the fields with a sack of freshly milled flour and a jar of home-pickled chive blossoms.

name: 汉弩库
Han Crossbow Vault
before: 古道尽头，一段被沙土封住的老路通向一座半埋的石库，门楣上刻着「河西弩库」。一伙精悍的大漠响马挖开了门，听说千里号把账本藏在了这里，进去翻了三天，账本没找到，倒翻出了汉朝的连弩，正擦着锈试射，箭能钉穿门板。

At the end of the old road, a sand-choked track leads to a half-buried stone vault, its lintel carved 'Hexi Crossbow Armoury'. A tough band of desert raiders dug it open, having heard the Qianli caravan hid its ledger here. Three days of searching found no ledger, only Han-dynasty repeating crossbows, which they're scrubbing and test-firing; the bolts go clean through a door plank.
after: 响马被打出了石库。账本果然不在，只在库门内侧找到一个粉笔画的记号：一个「千」字，一支箭头指向西边，旁边写着「已查，无人」。像是当年商队在这里找过什么人。你们带走能用的弩，把库门重新封上。

The raiders are driven out. No ledger, of course; only a chalk mark inside the door: the character Qian, an arrow pointing west, and beside it, 'Checked. Nobody here.' As though the caravan had once searched this place for someone. You take what crossbows still work and seal the door again.

name: 岩画洞
Painted Cave
before: 山脚有个浅洞，洞壁上满是古人画的岩画：猎人、黄羊、骑马的人。附近的孩子说，岩画里的人夜里会动，还会冒烟。大人们不信，可最近确实丢了不少东西。你们夜里摸过去，洞里果然有火光，岩画上的人影一晃一晃。

A shallow cave at the foot of the hills is covered in ancient paintings: hunters, gazelles, horsemen. The local children swear the painted people move at night, and sometimes smoke. The adults don't believe it, but plenty has gone missing lately. You creep up at night, and sure enough, firelight flickers inside and the figures sway.
after: 是一伙沙匪躲在洞里分赃，火光把岩画照得像在动。沙匪跑了，你们举着火把细看，古人的猎手旁边多了一长串新画的小人，一个牵一个往西走，数下来正好三百。最后一个小人回过头，手里拿着一本书。

It was a gang of sand bandits dividing loot, their fire making the paintings dance. They run. Looking closely by torchlight, you find a newer painting beside the ancient hunters: a long line of little figures, hand in hand, walking west. Exactly three hundred. The last one looks back, holding a book.

name: 乱烽墩
False Beacon
before: 长城边的一座烽火台，三天两头冒狼烟，关里的守军跑来好几趟，每次都扑个空。原来是一伙兵痞占了烽台，点假烽火把守军引走，再去抢关下的商铺。守军已经不信这座烽台了，说它是「放羊的孩子」。

A beacon tower by the wall sends up wolf-smoke every few days. The garrison has rushed out several times, always to find nothing. A gang of rogue soldiers holds the tower, lighting false alarms to draw the garrison off while they loot the shops below. The garrison no longer trusts this beacon; they call it 'the boy who cried wolf'.
after: 兵痞被赶下了烽台。老烽卒说，这座烽台上一次点真火是十年前：千里号出关，朝廷让沿路烽燧一站站点平安火送他们，一直传到阳关。「阳关那头的人，那时候就知道他们要来了。」你们又点了一把真火，往西传去。

The soldiers are driven off. The old beacon keeper says the last true fire here was ten years ago: when the Qianli caravan left, the court had every beacon light a fire of safe passage, relayed tower to tower all the way to Yangguan. 'Whoever was at Yangguan knew they were coming.' You light one honest fire, and it passes west.

name: 残棋坡
Unfinished Game
before: 坡上一块平石刻着棋盘，棋子摆了一半。一伙沙匪的头领是个棋痴，抓了过路人不抢东西，只逼着下棋，赢了放行，输了留下行李。可这盘棋他不许人碰：十年前一个拿算盘的商人跟他下到这里，说「回来再下完」。他天天擦这盘棋。

A chessboard is carved into a flat rock on the slope, pieces half set out. The bandit chief here is chess-mad: he doesn't rob captives, he makes them play. Win and pass; lose and leave your baggage. But this one game nobody may touch. Ten years ago a merchant with an abacus played him to this point and said, 'We'll finish when I'm back.' He polishes the board every day.
after: 头领输了，带你们看那盘残棋，叹口气：「那账房棋下得极好，偏偏这一步算错了，弃了车，后面全是死局。我问他是不是看走眼了，他说不是看走眼，是算错了账。」他把棋子收进袋子交给你们：「替我问问他，现在算明白没有。」

The chief loses and shows you the unfinished game with a sigh. 'That bookkeeper played beautifully, but this one move he miscalculated: gave up his chariot, and everything after was lost. I asked if he'd overlooked it. He said no. He'd got his sums wrong.' He bags the pieces and hands them to you. 'Ask him for me whether he's worked it out yet.'

name: 芦湾火药窖
Reed Bend Powder Cellar
before: 疏勒河拐弯处的芦苇荡里藏着一个地窖，一个恶霸养了一队精锐护院守着，夜里常有人看见窖口冒火星。窖里存着二十箱烟花，是十年前关里的商会凑钱买的，说好千里号回来那天在河边放。恶霸打算把烟花拆了，取火药去卖给沙匪。

In the reeds at a bend of the Shule River lies a cellar guarded by a bully's crack household troops; sparks are often seen at its mouth at night. Inside are twenty crates of fireworks, bought ten years ago by the merchants' guild inside the pass, to be set off by the river the day the Qianli caravan came home. The bully plans to strip out the powder and sell it to the bandits.
after: 护院们被打散了。二十箱烟花一箱没少，箱上贴着红纸：「千里号凯旋之日燃放」，纸都褪成了粉色。你们把箱子重新封好，留了一箱带在身上。总有一天用得上。

The guards are broken up. All twenty crates are intact, each pasted with red paper: 'To be lit on the day the Qianli caravan returns in triumph', faded now to pink. You reseal them and take one crate along. Someday you'll need it.

name: 戏台坡
Stage Slope
before: 坡下搭着一座草台，一个走江湖的戏班被两伙沙匪夹在中间：东边的要他们唱《千里号出关》，西边的偏要听《千里号遇鬼》，谁唱错了一出就砸谁的箱子。班主急得满头汗，说这两出戏其实是一出，只是没人知道结尾。

A makeshift stage stands at the foot of the slope, and a travelling opera troupe is caught between two gangs of sand bandits. The eastern gang demands 'The Qianli Caravan Leaves the Pass'; the western gang insists on 'The Qianli Caravan Meets a Ghost'. Sing the wrong one and your trunks get smashed. The troupe master, sweating, says they're really one play; it's just that nobody knows the ending.
after: 两伙沙匪都被打跑了。班主拉着你们问：「你们是往西去找他们的吧？找到了，回来告诉我们结尾。」他说戏班会一直唱前半出，唱到有人把后半出带回来为止。

Both gangs are driven off. The troupe master grabs your sleeve: 'You're going west to find them, aren't you? When you do, come back and tell us the ending.' The troupe will keep performing the first half, he says, until someone brings back the second.

name: 芦花滩
Reed Flat
before: 疏勒河边一片芦苇，芦花白得像雪。摆渡的老汉有个闺女，撑船比男人还稳。这几个月船过河心时总有人从水下割断缆绳，渡客都说河里有水鬼。闺女不信邪，夜里守在芦苇荡里，要看看水鬼长什么样。

Reeds line the Shule River here, plumes white as snow. The old ferryman has a daughter who poles a boat steadier than any man. For months someone has been cutting the tow rope from underwater at midstream, and passengers say a water ghost lives in the river. The daughter doesn't believe it and hides in the reeds at night to see one.
after: 水鬼被揪了出来：几个叼着芦管潜水的沙匪。闺女一篙子敲在为首那个的脑门上。她说她八岁那年，帮爹撑船送千里号过河，有个账房先生没给她船钱，给了她一颗糖，说「先欠着，回来给你两颗」。「我现在吃糖不稀罕了，」她撇撇嘴，「可他得回来。」

You drag out the 'ghosts': sand bandits breathing through reed straws. The daughter cracks the leader on the head with her pole. When she was eight, she says, she helped her father ferry the Qianli caravan across, and a bookkeeper gave her a sweet instead of the fare: 'I owe you. Two when I'm back.' 'I don't care about sweets any more,' she pouts. 'But he has to come back.'

name: 疏勒官渡
Shule Ferry Market
before: 疏勒河上唯一的官渡，河东是采石场，河西是红柳林，从前两岸隔河做买卖：东岸的石料过河，西岸的木料回来。如今渡口被一伙沙匪霸着，渡船拴在他们的营寨边，官秤被扔进了河里。两岸的人隔着水喊了半年，一笔生意也做不成。

The only official ferry on the Shule River. The east bank has quarries, the west bank tamarisk woods, and the two used to trade across the water: stone going west, timber coming back. Now sand bandits hold the landing, the ferries are moored by their stockade and the official scale lies at the bottom of the river. For half a year the banks have shouted across the water without a single deal.
after: 沙匪被赶下了河，渡船重新开动。老渡工从河底捞起官秤，两岸的生意重新做了起来：石料过河，木料回来。他翻出渡簿，指着十年前的一行字：「千里号，三百人，渡资欠，后补。」那一路，账房先生留下的欠条从玉门一直排到了这里，每一张都写着「后补」。老渡工说：「他欠的都记着，可他自己的账本呢？」

The bandits are driven into the river and the ferries run again. The old ferryman fishes up the scale and trade resumes: stone west, timber back. He opens the ferry register at a line from ten years ago: 'Qianli caravan. 300 people. Fare owed, to be paid later.' All the way from Yumen to here, the bookkeeper's IOUs line the road, every one saying 'to be paid later'. 'He wrote down everything he owed,' says the ferryman. 'But where's his own ledger?'
